# Japan’s Autumn Foliage Forecast 2026: Peak Times for Red and Yellow Leaves
## North to South, High to Low
From late autumn to early winter, the leaves on Japan’s deciduous trees turn bright colors, delighting onlookers, before they fall to the ground. Unlike the cherry blossom front, which moves northward in spring, the transformation to autumn foliage gradually spreads southward from Hokkaidō, and from higher ground to the cities below.

According to the September 2 forecast by the Japan Meteorological Corporation, due to high temperatures across the country, red and yellow foliage will peak somewhat later in 2026 than in a typical year.

Autumn foliage begins much earlier in high mountain areas than in lowland cities. Meanwhile, at the summit of Tokyo’s Mount Takao (599 meters) the leaves reach their best around November 6–20.

web.description:
If you're timing a trip around the Japan autumn leaves forecast 2026, here's the short answer: the Japan Meteorological Corporation published its first 2026 forecast on **September 2**, and it calls for peak red foliage in **Tokyo on November 29**, **Osaka on December 4** and **Kyoto on December 11** — all three inside JMC's "average" band; the clearly late cities are in Hokkaido and the mountains (Sapporo +10 days, Nagano +9). For first-time routes through Tokyo, Hakone and Kyoto, that puts the safest window in **late November to mid-December**.

Why it's hard to give one date: the colors sweep **southward** (and from higher ground down), reaching Tokyo in late November and Kansai from late November into mid-December in a typical year (JMC's 2026 call has Kyoto's peak from December 11 — a few days behind its average, still inside JMC's "average" band) and continuing into mid-December in Kyushu.

### 🍁 Quick Answer: Japan Autumn Leaves 2026
- **JMC first forecast (Sept 2):** Tokyo Nov 29 · Osaka Dec 4 · Kyoto Dec 11 · Nagoya Dec 2 · Sapporo Nov 7.
- **Safest window (Tokyo/Hakone/Kyoto):** late November to mid-December 2026.
- **Go early (Hokkaido/Tohoku/Nikko/Alps):** late September – mid-October.
- **Forecast:** Japan Meteorological Corporation (JMC) — first 2026 release out September 2; next update early October, then roughly monthly to late November.
- **Heads-up:** warm autumns pushed 2024–2025 peaks 1–2 weeks late — build in flexibility, especially for Kyoto.

### JMC's First 2026 Autumn Leaves Forecast: City by City
The Japan Meteorological Corporation released its first 2026 forecast on September 2. Its headline: autumn temperatures are expected to run above average nationwide, so peak colour will be **average or later than average** in most of the country. JMC flags only Sapporo and Nagano as "later than average"; every other city — Kyoto's +6 days included — sits inside its "average" band. Dates below are the forecast start of peak red foliage ( _momiji_); the next update is scheduled for early October and this page will be revised the same day.

| City | 2026 forecast | Average | vs. average (JMC verdict) |
|-|-|-|-|
| Sapporo | **Nov 7** | Oct 28 | +10 days — later than average |
| Aomori | **Nov 13** | Nov 13 | 0 — average |
| Sendai | **Nov 25** | Nov 21 | +4 days — average |
| Nagano | **Nov 21** | Nov 12 | +9 days — later than average |
| Tokyo | **Nov 29** | Nov 28 | +1 day — average |
| Kanazawa | **Nov 30** | Nov 24 | +6 days — average |
| Nagoya | **Dec 2** | Nov 28 | +4 days — average |
| Kyoto | **Dec 11** | Dec 5 | +6 days — average |
| Osaka | **Dec 4** | Dec 1 | +3 days — average |
| Hiroshima | **Nov 28** | Nov 22 | +6 days — average |
| Fukuoka | **Dec 7** | Dec 1 | +6 days — average |

## How the Japan Autumn Foliage Forecast 2026 Works
Unlike cherry blossoms (which move north), autumn foliage spreads **southward from Hokkaido** and from higher ground to the cities below — a slow wave rolling down the country over about two and a half months, from mid-September in northern Hokkaido to mid-December in southern Kyushu. The Japanese word for leaf-watching is _momijigari_ ("red-leaf hunting"); the colors themselves are _koyo_ or _momiji_.

The most-watched predictions come from the **Japan Meteorological Corporation (JMC)**, a private weather company. It estimates the "first day most of a sample tree's leaves turn red (or yellow)," tracking two waves separately: **yellow ginkgo** (late October) and **red maple** (early November). So chasing golden ginkgo in Tokyo means arriving a bit earlier than someone targeting deep-red maple temples in Kyoto. JMC's navigator covers roughly **700 viewing locations**, in multiple languages including English, with around four updates as the season unfolds.

## Why the 2026 Forecast Is Harder to Nail Than Usual
In **2024**, record September heat pushed red foliage in Tokyo to **December 5** (tying the latest date ever) and Osaka to December 8; of 51 observed cities, 11 were predicted to set new "latest-ever" records. Late-November travelers showed up to green leaves in Kyoto.

The first 2026 JMC forecast, out September 2, points the same way: above-average autumn temperatures and peaks running average-to-late in most cities, with Kyoto at December 11.

![Illuminated yukitsuri rope structures on pine trees reflected in a pond at Kenrokuen Garden, Kanazawa, during autumn](https://selfguidejapan.com/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fimages.selfguidejapan.com%2Fblog%2Fjapan-autumn-leaves-forecast-2026-kenrokuen.jpg&w=3840&q=75)Kenrokuen Garden, Kanazawa — one of Japan's finest autumn gardens, and a destination that books out fast once the season nears.

## Region-by-Region Timing for Autumn 2026
#### 🍂 Peak foliage windows by region (long-run pattern)
| Region | Peak window | Standout spots |
|-|-|-|
| Hokkaido | mid-Sep – late Oct | Daisetsuzan/Asahidake, Sounkyo, Jozankei; Sapporo early Nov |
| Tohoku | early Oct – mid-Nov | Oirase Gorge & Lake Towada, Yamadera, Kakunodate |
| Nikko | early Oct – mid-Nov | Yumoto/Chugushi (Oct), Lake Chuzenji (mid-Oct), town (late Nov) |
| Japanese Alps / central | mid-Oct – mid-Nov | Kamikochi, Tateyama Kurobe, Shirakawa-go; Kenrokuen later |
| Mt. Fuji / Kawaguchiko | early – late Nov | Maple Corridor (festival Nov 7–29, illuminated to 21:00) |
| Tokyo | late Nov – early Dec (JMC 2026: Nov 29) | Rikugien, Koishikawa Korakuen, Meiji Jingu Gaien ginkgo, Mt. Takao |
| Hiroshima / Miyajima | mid – late Nov | Momijidani Park (~700 maples) at the foot of Mt. Misen |

First colour arrives roughly a month to six weeks ahead of peak: mid-September in Hokkaido, early October in Tohoku and the Alps, early November across Kanto, Kansai and the Setouchi, and mid-November in Kyushu.

JMC's first 2026 forecast (September 2, covering more than 700 viewing spots) runs a few days behind the long-run averages in most cities — still inside JMC's "average" band everywhere except Sapporo and Nagano — see the city table near the top of this page. JMC updates roughly monthly through late November; the next release is due in early October, and this page is revised the same day.

## FAQ: Japan Autumn Leaves Forecast 2026
When is the best time to visit Japan for autumn foliage in 2026? expand_more

For most first-time routes (Tokyo, Hakone, Kyoto), late November to mid-December 2026: JMC's first forecast puts Tokyo at November 29 and Kyoto at December 11. Go earlier — late September to mid-October — for Hokkaido, Tohoku, Nikko or the Japanese Alps.

When does the official 2026 fall foliage forecast come out? expand_more

It is out: the Japan Meteorological Corporation released its first 2026 forecast on September 2, 2026. The next update is scheduled for early October, then roughly monthly through late November.

Will the 2026 season be late again? expand_more

Slightly, and mostly in Hokkaido and the mountains. JMC expects above-average autumn temperatures; it flags Sapporo (November 7, ten days late) and Nagano (November 21, nine days late) as later than average, while Tokyo (November 29), Osaka (December 4) and Kyoto (December 11, six days behind its average) all sit inside JMC's "average" band.

expand_more

Yes, at higher elevations — Asahidake (the highest peak of Daisetsuzan) can begin in mid-September. Lower cities like Sapporo peak late October to early November.

How long does peak foliage last in one spot? expand_more

Usually about 1–2 weeks, occasionally longer if it stays cool; an early frost or windstorm can cut it short. Across a region, the peak can span two weeks to more than a month.

What's the difference between koyo and momiji? expand_more

Both mean autumn leaves. Koyo (紅葉) is the general term; momiji specifically points to Japanese maples and the pastime of viewing them — momijigari is the autumn cousin of hanami.

### Turn the Forecast Into a Route
Reading forecasts is one thing; turning them into a working itinerary with trains, ryokan and backup plans is another. We match your dates to the regions most likely to be peaking, build in flexibility around the JMC updates, and steer you clear of the worst crowd traps.

## When is Fall Foliage in Japan?
The fall season in Japan spans from mid-September to early December. Tokyo and Kyoto typically experience the best views from mid-October to early December, and Kyushu's fall colors are most vibrant toward the end of November.

![Japan Fall Foliage 2026 Forecast](https://www.japanshoreexcursions.com/wp-content/uploads/Japan-Fall-Foliage-2026-Forecast-.jpg)

Unlike the unpredictable cherry blossoms, autumn in Japan offers a more extended and predictable period for enjoying fall colors. This allows for easier planning around the vibrant autumn scenery.

| DESTINATION | BEST TIME | AVERAGE |
|-|-|-|
| Hokkaido (Sapporo, Kushiro, Asahikawa, Daisetsuzan) | Late Sep - Late Oct | 15 Oct 2026 |
| Tohoku (Sendai, Akita, Aomori) | Mid Oct - Early Nov | 25 Oct 2026 |
| Chubu (Nagano, Kanazawa, Mt. Fuji) | Late Oct - Mid Nov | 3 Nov 2026 |
| Kanto (Tokyo, Hakone) | Mid Nov - Early Dec | 23 Nov 2026 |
| Kansai (Kyoto, Osaka, Nara) | Late Nov - Early Dec | 30 Nov 2026 |
| Chugoku (Hiroshima, Okayama) | Mid Nov - Early Dec | 23 Nov 2026 |
| Shikoku (Kochi) | Mid Nov - Late Nov | 20 Nov 2026 |
| Okinawa (Okinawa, Naha) | N/A | N/A |

Japan Fall Foliage Forecast 2026

**Best Viewing Period:** Early November to early December

### Lake Ashi, Hakone
**Best Viewing Period:** Early November to the end of November

In the nearby Senjōgahara Grassy Plain, the vegetation gradually shifts to yellow and orange by late September, complementing the distant Mt.

# Japan's Autumn Foliage Forecast for 2026
Get your travel plans lined up with these early estimates

![Kim Bergström](https://a3.cdn.japantravel.com/photo/807584090-1034371/300x300%21/1034371.webp)

By [Kim Bergström](https://en.japantravel.com/profile/kim-b/807584090)

Japan Travel Staff

The first signs of autumn are officially on the horizon in Japan, with the Japan Meteorological Corporation (JMC) releasing its first forecast for the 2026 fall foliage season on September 2.

The forecast covers around 700 popular foliage-viewing locations across Japan, from Hokkaido all the way down to Kagoshima. JMC also provides forecasts for around 3,000 mountains, with predictions taking altitude into account, which can be particularly useful for travelers hoping to catch the changing colors at higher elevations.

![Photo: Sora Sagano / Unsplash](https://a0.cdn.japantravel.com/photo/72752-1098575/630x420%21/autumn-foliage-2026-1098575.webp)

Photo: [Sora Sagano](https://unsplash.com/photos/body-of-water-surrounded-by-trees-4T_74DQL3qg) / Unsplash

## Red and Yellow
There are actually two different foliage forecasts to keep an eye on: red leaves, primarily maple trees, and yellow leaves, including ginkgo trees. The two don't necessarily peak at the same time, so knowing both can help when planning an autumn itinerary.

According to the first 2026 forecast, red maple leaves are expected to reach their viewing peak in Tokyo around November 29, Kyoto around December 11, Osaka around December 4, and Fukuoka around December 7.

For yellow ginkgo leaves, the forecast is slightly earlier, with Tokyo expected around November 26, Kyoto November 27, Osaka November 24, and Fukuoka November 27.

![Photo: Tsuyoshi Kozu / Unsplash](https://a1.cdn.japantravel.com/photo/72752-1098574/630x420%21/autumn-foliage-2026-1098574.webp)

Photo: [Tsuyoshi Kozu](https://unsplash.com/photos/yellow-trees-line-a-road-in-autumn-6vZNCjVFlWU) / Unsplash

Further north, the season starts much earlier. Sapporo's red leaves are forecast for around November 7, while Aomori is expected around November 13. In Nagano, red leaves are forecast for November 21.

At the other end of the country, Kagoshima's red leaves aren't expected until around December 10.

These dates aren't set in stone. Just like the sakura forecasts, foliage predictions can be refined as the season gets closer based on weather conditions and temperatures. Still, the first forecast provides a handy starting point for anyone planning a Japan trip around autumn colors.

JMC's next foliage forecast is scheduled for early October, when travelers should have a clearer picture of how the season is shaping up.
